# Belmont Glass Works

Belmont Glass Works, also known as the Belmont Glass Company, was one of Ohio's early glassmaking companies that operated from 1865 to 1890 . The company was named after Belmont County, Ohio, where the plant was located in the riverfront village of Bellaire . As the first glass factory in Bellaire, Belmont Glass Works played a significant role in establishing the region's reputation as a center for glass manufacturing .

## History

### Founding and Early Years

Belmont Glass Works was founded in 1865, with production beginning in 1866 . The company was established by experienced glass makers, several of whom were former employees of the Hobbs works in Wheeling, West Virginia . Among the key founders was John Robinson, a Civil War veteran who had previously worked at the Hobbs, Brockunier & Company glass works in Wheeling . Other important figures in the company included Henry Faupel, Charles Henry Over, and Henry Crimmel .

The location of the factory in Bellaire, Ohio, was strategically chosen due to the area's abundant natural resources and transportation advantages. Bellaire had coal deposits, railroad service, and access to the Ohio River, making it an ideal location for glass manufacturing . The company began operations in a riverfront village along the east side of Belmont County .

### Growth and Expansion

Belmont Glass Works quickly became a significant employer in the region. By 1884, the company had grown to employ 350 workers . The factory initially focused on producing glass chimneys but later transitioned to manufacturing pressed glassware . This shift in production helped establish the company as a major player in the growing glass industry of the Ohio River Valley.

The company's success contributed to Bellaire's emergence as a prominent glass manufacturing center. By 1881, Bellaire had 15 glass factories and had earned the nickname "Glass City" . Ohio was a leading state in glass production during this period, and Belmont County was particularly important to the industry .

### Decline and Closure

Several factors contributed to the eventual decline and closure of Belmont Glass Works. In 1876, the company experienced a significant loss of talent when three key employees—John Robinson, C. H. Over, and William Gorby—left to establish their own glassworks . This departure weakened the company's leadership and technical expertise.

The company continued operations despite these challenges, but eventually closed in 1890 following an economic recession . The closure of Belmont Glass Works marked the end of an era for one of Ohio's pioneering glass manufacturing companies.

## Products and Patterns

Belmont Glass Works produced a variety of glass products, primarily focusing on lamps and bar goods . The company was particularly known for its pressed glassware, which featured several distinctive patterns that became popular in the late 19th century.

One of the most notable patterns produced by Belmont Glass Works was the "Daisy & Button" (or "Daisy Button") pattern . This pattern was produced in both crystal and colored glass and included items such as cruet sets, berry bowls, and other tableware . The Daisy & Button pattern was highly collectible and is still sought after by antique glass collectors today.

Another significant product was the "Russian Sleigh" pattern, which was introduced in 1886 . The original Russian Sleigh made by Belmont Glass Works was 11 inches long . This decorative item was likely produced as a novelty or special-order piece rather than as part of a regular tableware line.

The company also produced the "Grasshopper without Insect" pattern, examples of which date from 1898 . This pattern was used on covered bowls and other decorative items. Additionally, Belmont Glass Works manufactured oil lamps with pattern #120, also known as the "Reflecting Fans" pattern .

Belmont Glass Works also produced depression glass items, including a green depression glass berry bowl with a bowknot pattern . The company's products were distributed throughout the United States and were known for their quality craftsmanship and innovative designs.

## Legacy

Although Belmont Glass Works operated for only 24 years, its legacy extended far beyond its years of operation. Many of the company's former employees went on to become prominent figures in the glass industry . The Crimmel brothers—Henry, Jacob, and John—who had worked at Belmont Glass Works, later became well-known glassmakers in Ohio and Indiana .

The skills and techniques developed at Belmont Glass Works influenced the entire Ohio River Valley glass industry. The company's transition from producing glass chimneys to pressed glassware helped establish new standards for glass manufacturing in the region .

Today, items produced by Belmont Glass Works are highly collectible and can be found in museums and private collections worldwide. The Iowa State University Museums houses several pieces from Belmont Glass Works in its Iowa Quester Glass Collection . These artifacts provide valuable insights into the company's production methods and design aesthetic.

The site of the original Belmont Glass Works in Bellaire, Ohio, is now part of the National Imperial Glass Museum, which celebrates the rich glassmaking heritage of the region . The museum preserves the history of glass manufacturing in Bellaire, including the story of Belmont Glass Works and its contributions to the industry.

**Belmont County** is a county located in the state of [Ohio](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ohio "Ohio") in the [United States](https://kids.kiddle.co/United_States "United States"). In 2020, about 66,497 people lived here. The main town, called the [county seat](https://kids.kiddle.co/County_seat "County seat"), is [St. Clairsville](https://kids.kiddle.co/St._Clairsville,_Ohio "St. Clairsville, Ohio"). The biggest city in the county is [Martins Ferry](https://kids.kiddle.co/Martins_Ferry,_Ohio "Martins Ferry, Ohio"). Belmont County was officially started in 1801. Its name comes from a [French](https://kids.kiddle.co/French_language "French language") phrase meaning "beautiful mountain." It is also part of the larger Wheeling metropolitan area.

History of Belmont County
-------------------------

Belmont County was created in September 1801. It was formed from parts of [Jefferson](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jefferson_County,_Ohio "Jefferson County, Ohio") and [Washington](https://kids.kiddle.co/Washington_County,_Ohio "Washington County, Ohio") counties. Two months later, it was officially organized. [St. Clairsville](https://kids.kiddle.co/St._Clairsville,_Ohio "St. Clairsville, Ohio") became the county seat in 1803.

Over time, parts of Belmont County were used to form other counties. In 1810, some land went to [Guernsey County](https://kids.kiddle.co/Guernsey_County,_Ohio "Guernsey County, Ohio"). In 1813, more land was used for [Monroe County](https://kids.kiddle.co/Monroe_County,_Ohio "Monroe County, Ohio"). Since 1813, the county's borders have stayed the same. The name _Belmont_ means "beautiful mountain" in French.

Early settlers came to the county using paths like [Zane's Trace](https://kids.kiddle.co/Zane%27s_Trace "Zane's Trace"). Later, the National Road was built through the area. Many of the first settlers were [Quakers](https://kids.kiddle.co/Quakers "Quakers"). These people were strong opponents of slavery. One famous abolitionist, [Benjamin Lundy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Benjamin_Lundy "Benjamin Lundy"), was among them.

### Coal and Glass Industries

Belmont County is in Ohio's coal region. Long ago, steamships on the [Ohio River](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ohio_River "Ohio River") would stop in Bellaire for coal. By 1866, railroads also served the county. These transportation links, along with coal and skilled workers, made the county a great place for glass factories.

The first glass factory was Excelsior Glass Works, started in 1849. In 1866, Belmont Glass Company opened in Bellaire. It was the first of many glass plants there. Bellaire became known as "Glass City" because it had 15 glass factories by 1881. Ohio was a leading state in glass production, and Belmont County was very important to this industry.

### Fun Events and Symbols

Belmont County was home to the famous Jamboree in the Hills. This outdoor country music festival took place every year from 1977 to 2018. In 1986, the county held a special election. People voted for a new official county seal and flag. These were designed by Michael Massa, who lived in the county.

Geography of Belmont County
---------------------------

[![Image 9: Geography of Ohio - DPLA - aaba7b3295ff6973b6fd1e23e33cde14 (page 83) (cropped)](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/c/c4/Geography_of_Ohio_-_DPLA_-_aaba7b3295ff6973b6fd1e23e33cde14_%28page_83%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/300px-Geography_of_Ohio_-_DPLA_-_aaba7b3295ff6973b6fd1e23e33cde14_%28page_83%29_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Geography_of_Ohio_-_DPLA_-_aaba7b3295ff6973b6fd1e23e33cde14_(page_83)_(cropped).jpg)

Coal miners in Belmont County, 1923

Belmont County is located on the eastern side of Ohio. Its eastern border is next to [West Virginia](https://kids.kiddle.co/West_Virginia "West Virginia"), across the [Ohio River](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ohio_River "Ohio River"). The Ohio River flows south along the county's eastern edge. Captina Creek and McMahon Creek also flow through the county. They both empty into the Ohio River.

The county has gentle, rolling hills with many small streams. Most of the land is used for farming. The highest point in the county is Galloway Knob, which is about 1,396 feet (426 meters) above sea level. The county covers a total area of about 541 square miles (1492 square kilometers). Most of this is land, with a small part being water.

According to the 2010 United States census, there were 70,400 people living in Belmont County. About 28,679 households were counted. The population density was about 132 people per square mile. Most of the people living in the county were white (94.0%). About 4.0% were black or African American.

The average age of people in the county was 43.4 years old. About 27.2% of households had children under 18 living with them. The average household had 2.32 people.

 Collection Info 

![Image 2: Iowa Quester Glass Collection](https://emuseum.its.iastate.edu/internal/media/dispatcher/22482/preview)

The Iowa Quester Glass Collection now numbers over 1,000 objects ranging from monumental Brilliant Period cut glass to colorful art glass and a diverse array of Early American Pattern Glass. This unique collection, housed in and cared for by Iowa State University Museums, Ames, Iowa, showcases American glass from 1840 to 1950.

In 1996, a partnership was formed between the Iowa Questers led by Kay Beckett of the Neta Snook Chapter in Ames, then Iowa Questers’ State President, Shirley Foster, and University Museums’ director, Lynette Pohlman. At that time, the University Museums was known nationally for having an encyclopedic glass collection as recognized by scholars and the pre-eminent American glass museum, the Corning Museum of Glass of Corning, NY. After a vote from the Iowa Quester State Council the Iowa Quester Glass Collection was formalized with the following mission: “To establish an Iowa Questers Glass Collection, of historic glass from around the world, at Iowa State University Museums. This would provide a State of Iowa resource for preserving, viewing and interpreting historic glass objects. The focus will be on American-made glass from 1840-1945.”

Now the bulk of the collection is American pressed glass pre-Depression Era most of which would fall under the Early American Pressed Glass (EAPG) group. Iconic works of glass include a Jumbo pattern table set, many pieces of Iowa City and Keota glass, a Rebecca at the Well tall standard compote, Terrestrial Globe pattern butter dish, examples from historical glass, the state’s series, and novelties. Thoughtful gifting of three major pressed glass collections just this past two years included over 130 toothpick holders, dozens of whale oil lamps, and a collection of 50+ sauce dishes and other glass works. With the help of many chapters, individuals, partners and collaborators, the collection continues to grow by leaps and bounds!

About
-----

Known for its early handmade glass tableware, the Imperial Glass Company, a.k.a. "The Big I," manufactured glassware for 80 years in the town of Bellaire, [Ohio](https://www.atlasobscura.com/things-to-do/ohio). The Imperial Glass Collectors' Society established this museum in 2003 to keep its legacy alive in the area.

The Imperial Glass Company was founded in the Ohio River town of Bellaire, and the factory started producing handmade glass in 1904. It became a success early on, thanks to its intricate patterns and variety of price points. The company would later be known for its innovative lines of glass such as Candlewick, Free Hand, and Lead Lustre.

In later years, Imperial Glass faced tough competition from cheaper imports and a slowing economy. The company was ultimately dissolved in 1984 after several buyouts and the factory was bulldozed to make way for a shopping wall.
